grandplace: Brussels' main square, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: around the cobbles stand the guild houses with their gilded façades, the Maison du Roi (now the City Museum) and the Gothic Town Hall with its tower, nearly a hundred metres high.
galeries: One of Europe's first covered shopping arcades, opened in 1847: three glass-roofed passages with historic cafés, chocolatiers and bookshops. You can walk through in a few minutes, but it's worth slowing down.
manneken: The bronze statuette of a little boy peeing, the city's irreverent symbol: it's much smaller than you'd imagine. He has a wardrobe of hundreds of costumes, worn on set dates: the nearby GardeRobe MannekenPis displays some of them.
stgery: Saint-Géry, Sainte-Catherine and the Black Tower

The lively centre west of the Grand-Place: Place Saint-Géry with the old Halles, bars and terraces, and further north Place Sainte-Catherine with its church and the Black Tower, a 13th-century bastion of the medieval walls still standing among the buildings.
cathedrale: Cathedral of St Michael and St Gudula
The Gothic cathedral on the hill above the station, with two square towers and large stained-glass windows. It's where Belgium's great ceremonies are held.
bd: The museum of Belgian comics, in a former warehouse designed by Victor Horta: Tintin, the Smurfs, Lucky Luke and many more, told through original artwork and the story of how the characters were born. The city also has dozens of comic-strip murals to see for free as you walk.
montdesarts: Mont des Arts and Parc de Bruxelles

The terraced gardens climbing from Central Station to the upper town, with a fine view over the centre and the Town Hall tower. At the top are Place Royale and the Parc de Bruxelles, the big park facing the Royal Palace.
musees: Royal Museums of Fine Arts and Magritte Museum

A complex of museums around Place Royale: the Magritte Museum has the world's largest collection of the Surrealist painter's work, and the Oldmasters Museum shows Flemish masters such as Bruegel and Rubens. The Magritte alone fills a morning.
sablon: Sablon, Marolles and the Palace of Justice

The elegant quarter of antique dealers and chocolatiers, with the Gothic church of Notre-Dame du Sablon and the small Petit Sablon park. Further down begin the Marolles, the working-class quarter with the Place du Jeu de Balle flea market; up above, Place Poelaert has the gigantic Palace of Justice and a panoramic terrace over the city.
atomium: Brussels' modern symbol, built for the 1958 World's Fair: nine steel spheres joined by tubes, reproducing an iron crystal magnified billions of times. You enter five spheres with exhibitions and a viewpoint at the top; the ticket also includes the nearby Design Museum Brussels.
cinquantenaire: Cinquantenaire Park and the European Quarter

The great park created for the 1880 Exhibition, with its monumental triple arch, surrounded by museums and, a little further on, the European institutions' quarter with the European Parliament and the Parlamentarium.
